svg.title: SPACE & DevEx
svg.desc: SPACE & DevEx. Measure developer productivity without counting code: surveys and system data on satisfaction, flow, feedback loops and cognitive load. Step 1, Activity as productivity: 15 more engineers, no speed-up: a leaderboard counts commits and lines, not what slows work down. Step 2, SPACE: what to measure: SPACE: five dimensions, each with a survey and a system measure, read per team, never per person. Step 3, DevEx: fix the friction: DevEx finds the friction: CI at 38 min, 5 tools, broken-up days. Q3: CI 12 min, focus 3.1 h a day. Step 4, Pitfalls and limits: Pitfalls: ranking people, one score, ignored results, unlike teams compared, one kind of data.

g.text: 15 more engineers, no speed-up: a leaderboard counts commits and lines, not what slows work down.
SPACE: five dimensions, each with a survey and a system measure, read per team, never per person.
DevEx finds the friction: CI at 38 min, 5 tools, broken-up days. Q3: CI 12 min, focus 3.1 h a day.
Pitfalls: ranking people, one score, ignored results, unlike teams compared, one kind of data.
the leaderboard sees one of five dimensions
the board deck folds all five rows into
→ show the dimensions side by side
SPACE: no single metric captures it
✗ Only system data, or only survey data
the CI chart says 12 min, fixed; answers say
flaky tests force re-runs, so people still wait
→ read each kind against the other
DevEx: each kind misses what the other sees
the same survey asks where work gets stuck
what the Q2 survey found, and the fix
a team that never heard back
how fast builds, tests and reviews answer

waiting for CI: 38 min a run
the mental effort a task takes
asked: how hard is a new service?
being in the zone: deep, focused work
asked: how many hours can you focus?
search never heard back about its Q2
results, so in Q3 only 2 of its 6 answered
under 5 answers: no team result at all
fix one thing and say what changed
CTO: 15 more engineers, so where is the speed-up?
Manager: let’s rank everyone by commits, PRs and lines
nobody has asked the engineers what slows them down
Acme’s own numbers, not research findings
✗ Comparing teams that do different work
a slide ranks the teams on satisfaction and puts payments last,
but its changes wait for PCI approval: different work, not a worse team
DORA (2025): self-reported data compares poorly across teams
